tool.name: TimeStepLayoutExporter
tool.summary: Exports a layout once per step and stitches the frames into an animated GIF: month by month (or any hour, day, week, month or year step) through a date field, one frame per value of an attribute, one frame per layer, or one frame per bookmark. A layout text element with {STEP} in its text shows the step label in every frame. Frames can be kept with a manifest CSV. The project is never saved and everything the tool changes (definition queries, visibility, text, map frame extent and rotation) is restored.

param.name: project
param.dialogReference: The project (.aprx) to use. Leave empty to use the current project when the tool runs inside ArcGIS Pro. The tool never saves the project. Working on a saved copy is the safest choice.

param.name: layout_name
param.dialogReference: Name of the layout. Optional when the project has only one layout.

param.name: map_frame_name
param.dialogReference: Name of the map frame. Optional when the layout has only one.

param.name: mode
param.dialogReference: TIME (steps through a date field), ATTRIBUTE (one frame per value of a field), LAYER_VISIBILITY (one frame per listed layer) or BOOKMARKS (one frame per bookmark).

param.name: step_layers
param.dialogReference: Rows of layer name and field name. TIME: one or more layers with a date field. ATTRIBUTE: exactly one layer and field. A layer that is switched off, or inside a group that is switched off, is not drawn (the run warns).

param.name: start_time
param.dialogReference: TIME: first instant. Empty = earliest date in the data, rounded down to the step unit (to midnight for DAYS and WEEKS: a week step starts on the day of the earliest date, not on a fixed weekday).

param.name: end_time
param.dialogReference: TIME: last instant, included. A date without a time includes that whole day. Empty = latest date in the data.

param.name: interval
param.dialogReference: TIME: length of one step, in units (1 = every month).

param.name: interval_unit
param.dialogReference: TIME: HOURS, DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS or YEARS. Month and year steps follow the calendar (31 Jan, 28 Feb, 31 Mar).

param.name: window_type
param.dialogReference: SLIDING shows the last Window Steps steps; CUMULATIVE shows everything from the start up to the current step.

param.name: window_steps
param.dialogReference: Width of a sliding window, in steps (1 = only the current step).

param.name: label_format
param.dialogReference: TIME: format of the step label. Tokens %Y %y %m %d %H %M %S %b %B. Default depends on the unit (for months: %b %Y). The same format is used for {STEP} (the start of the step), {FROM} (the start of the window) and {TO} (the last second of the window); use {TO} to name the period a frame shows. Any other % token is copied as typed (the run warns).

param.name: label_language
param.dialogReference: EN or AR: language of month names in labels (digits stay Western).

param.name: value_order
param.dialogReference: ATTRIBUTE: ASCENDING or DESCENDING. Number fields are ordered by value (-10, -2, 0, 1.25, 1.5, 10); text in natural order (2 before 10), ignoring case. Values of a Single (float32) field are shown in their shortest form (1.1, not 1.100000023841858).

param.name: step_values
param.dialogReference: ATTRIBUTE: your own list of values in the order you want; values not listed get no frame. On a date field a value is read as a date (2025-01-01 = midnight; 02/01/2025 is month/day/year, 1 February) and matched to the second. On a number field a value is read as a number with a point as the decimal separator and matched by value (2, 2.0 and +2 are the same; 1.1 matches a Single field holding 1.1). A listed value that is not in the data gives a warning that names the form to use.

param.name: visibility_items
param.dialogReference: LAYER_VISIBILITY: layer or group layer names; a name listed twice is shown in both of its frames. BOOKMARKS: bookmark names (empty = all bookmarks); an exact name is matched first, and a name that matches two bookmarks only when case is ignored is refused.

param.name: text_element_name
param.dialogReference: Optional: change only the text element with this name. Empty = every text element that contains a placeholder.

param.name: resolution
param.dialogReference: Export resolution in dpi (default 96).

param.name: frame_ms
param.dialogReference: Duration of each frame in milliseconds (at least 20). The GIF stores delays in steps of 10 ms, so 25 is written as 20.

param.name: last_hold_ms
param.dialogReference: Duration of the last frame in milliseconds (the hold at the end).

param.name: loop_count
param.dialogReference: 0 = repeat forever. Other values are written as the GIF loop count; viewers differ in whether 1 means one or two plays.

param.name: palette_mode
param.dialogReference: GLOBAL: one palette for the whole sequence (no colour flicker). PER_FRAME: each frame has its own palette.

param.name: max_colours
param.dialogReference: Colours in the GIF palette, 2 to 256. Up to this number of colours in the whole sequence the palette is exact. With more colours the most frequent colours (page white, black text) are kept exactly and part of the palette is reserved for small saturated colours (legend swatches, symbols).

param.name: dither
param.dialogReference: Floyd-Steinberg dithering for frames whose colours do not fit the palette (off by default; dithering can make static areas flicker). It is never applied to a frame that fits the palette exactly: that would only add noise and turn the white page grey.

param.name: max_frames
param.dialogReference: Safety limit on the number of frames (default 300).

param.name: out_gif
param.dialogReference: Output animated GIF.

param.name: out_frames_folder
param.dialogReference: Optional folder in which the PNG frames are kept (created if missing). Other files in it are never deleted; frame files of an earlier run that this run does not replace are left in place and warned about. Without it the frames are deleted after the GIF is written.

param.name: out_manifest
param.dialogReference: Optional CSV with one row per frame: number, label, time range, detail, feature count, file, bytes and SHA-256. Text that Excel would run as a formula (starting with =, +, -, @) gets a leading apostrophe.

tool.usage:
NOT VERIFIED: the Basic licence, starting the tool from the Pro GUI, and the memory guard on a real page. Needs ArcGIS Pro (arcpy.mp) and, for the GIF only, Pillow (both are in ArcGIS Pro's Python; without Pillow the frames and manifest are still written when Output Frames Folder is set). No MP4 output is offered: no video encoder was found in the Pro 3.3.2 Python environment.

Time steps are made with a definition query on the date field of each step layer (the project's own Map Time settings are not used: MapFrame.time was None after enabling layer time in an arcpy-built project in ArcGIS Pro 3.3.2, and also in a saved and reopened project; a GUI-built project was not tried). The layer's own definition query is kept and combined with the step query.

In the layout, type a text such as 'Deliveries - {STEP}'. {STEP} is the step label, {FROM} and {TO} the first and last time (or value) of the window, {INDEX} and {COUNT} the frame number and the number of frames. Every text element that contains one of them is changed per frame and restored. In TIME mode {STEP} is the start of the step, not the period the frame shows: use {TO} (or {FROM} - {TO}) for that period, for example 'cumulative to {TO}' (quarterly steps of 2025, last frame: {STEP} = October 2025, {TO} = December 2025).
